title: Hierarchical Multi-Scale Molecular Conformer Generation
claim: Complex structures are organized hierarchically: a coarse core anchors the whole, and finer detail is added progressively to complete it.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dotted dividers, arrows between bottom labels
description: A three-panel horizontal strip showing the same molecule at increasing levels of detail, separated by thin dotted vertical lines. The left panel shows the bare scaffold: two disconnected ring fragments drawn as gray ball-and-stick, with blue nitrogen and yellow sulfur atoms. The middle panel shows the scaffold joined into one structure with side chains, with red oxygen atoms added. The right panel shows the final structure with all atoms, including small white hydrogens, rendered denser and more tangled. Below, bold serif labels read 'Scaffold → Functionalized Scaffold → Final Structure', joined by thick black arrows. The eye goes first to the colored atoms in the molecules, then follows the arrows left to right as complexity increases.
caption: Multi-Scale Molecule Representation.
abstract: Molecular conformer generation is a fundamental task for drug discovery and material design. Although deep generative models have progressed in this area, existing methods often overlook the hierarchical structural organization inherent to molecules, leading to poor-quality generated conformers. To address this challenge, we demonstrate that capturing the spatial arrangement of key substructures, such as scaffolds, is essential, as they serve as anchors that define the overall molecular distribution. In this paper, we propose a hierarchical multi-scale molecular conformer generation framework (MSGEN), designed to enhance key substructure awareness by leveraging spatially informed guidance. Our framework initiates the generation process from coarse-grained key substructures, progressively refining the conformer by utilizing these coarser-scale structures as conditional guidance for subsequent finer-scale stages. To bridge scale discrepancies between stages, we introduce a molecular upsampling technique that aligns the structural scales, ensuring smooth propagation of geometric guidance. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our framework integrates seamlessly with a wide range of existing molecular generative models and consistently generates more stable and chemically plausible molecular conformers.
